purpose: Coverage, concept, prerequisite, notation, and spiral-design advice only; this file does not create course or lesson artifacts.

design_constraints.learner: Busy engineer with algebra, trigonometry, and basic scripting, but no assumed prior DSP course.
design_constraints.core_shape: A gentle computational on-ramp followed by a representation-driven DSP spine; specialist depth remains skippable extras.

first_two_lessons.requirement: Both are intentionally the easiest lessons, introduce no transform notation, and end in a visible or audible result.
first_two_lessons.lesson_01_win: Plot, shift, scale, add, and compare a short sampled signal, then use a three-point running average supplied as a recipe to clean a noisy trace.
first_two_lessons.lesson_02_win: Synthesize a sampled sinusoid, change amplitude/frequency/phase, and hear and see one alias pair before any reconstruction theorem is stated.
guardrails: No calculus, complex arithmetic, convolution sum, or transform definition in lesson 01.
Lesson 02 uses the unit-circle animation only after the waveform is familiar and treats aliasing as an observation to explain later.
Formal sampling conditions, equality cases, and reconstruction arrive in lesson 07, correcting the primer's deliberately simplified statements.

design_constraints.advanced_boundary: Every advanced node is type extra, may depend on core nodes, and is absent from every core prerequisite list.

source_registry.role: Rigorous core for LTI systems, transforms, z-plane reasoning, DFT, structures, sampling, and filter design.
Engineer-facing intuition, numerical traces, implementation cautions, quadrature, multirate, and finite-word effects.
Authoritative advanced multirate, polyphase, perfect-reconstruction, filter-bank, and wavelet theory.
Broad computational backbone with executable algorithms, filter designs, multirate processing, STFT, and applications.
Gentle physical intuition, tool-building progression, implementation judgment, and broad applications.
Representation-first systems pedagogy, prediction checks, sampling/quantization, and application capstones.
Fourier/convolution/sampling derivations and continuous-to-discrete conceptual bridge.
Proof-conscious graduate DSP, misconceptions, spectral analysis, multirate structures, STFT, projects, and edge cases.
Statistical definition of spectra, nonparametric estimators, and optional parametric/subspace/spatial depth.
Windowing, audio spectra, STFT/WOLA, FFT convolution, filter-bank duality, measured audio, and repair-by-experiment pedagogy.
Canonical finite-record leakage, window metrics, and controlled unequal-tone comparison.
Primary-source FFT factorization, operation count, in-place staging, and bit-reversed ordering.
Visual no-prerequisite on-ramp for samples, sinusoids, DFT mechanics, zero padding, and leakage; requires formal qualification later.

concepts.name: Discrete-time sequence
concepts.definition: A value indexed by an integer sample number.

concepts.name: Sampled sinusoid
concepts.definition: A discrete waveform A cos(omega n + phi) characterized by amplitude, normalized frequency, and phase.

concepts.name: Sampling
concepts.definition: Mapping a continuous-time signal to values spaced by a sampling period.

concepts.name: Aliasing
concepts.definition: Indistinguishability created when distinct continuous or discrete frequencies produce the same samples after rate change.

concepts.name: Discrete-time system
concepts.definition: A mapping from an input sequence to an output sequence.

concepts.name: Linear time-invariant system
concepts.definition: A system obeying superposition and shift invariance.

concepts.name: Impulse response
concepts.definition: The output of an LTI system to the unit impulse, sufficient to characterize the system.

concepts.name: Linear convolution
concepts.definition: The weighted sum of shifted impulse responses that gives an LTI output.

concepts.name: Complex exponential
concepts.definition: A rotating phasor e^(j omega n) whose real and imaginary projections are sinusoids.

concepts.name: Frequency response
concepts.definition: The complex gain H(e^(j omega)) applied by an LTI system to a complex exponential.

concepts.name: Discrete-time Fourier transform
concepts.definition: A periodic continuous-frequency representation of a sequence.

concepts.name: z-transform
concepts.definition: A complex-variable sequence representation with an explicit region of convergence.

concepts.name: Poles, zeros, and stability
concepts.definition: z-plane geometry connecting roots, frequency response, causality, and bounded-input bounded-output stability.

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform
concepts.definition: N orthogonal frequency coefficients for an N-sample record.

concepts.name: Circular convolution
concepts.definition: Convolution modulo N, corresponding to multiplication of DFT coefficients.

concepts.name: Fast Fourier transform
concepts.definition: A factorized DFT evaluation requiring order N log N work for suitable lengths.

concepts.name: Analysis window
concepts.definition: A finite weighting applied before spectral analysis or frame processing.

concepts.name: Leakage-resolution tradeoff
concepts.definition: The exchange among main-lobe width, sidelobe behavior, amplitude bias, and noise bandwidth in finite records.

concepts.name: Random process model
concepts.definition: A probabilistic model for an indexed family of random variables, distinguished from one finite record.

concepts.name: Autocorrelation
concepts.definition: Expected similarity between a random process and a lagged copy.

concepts.name: Power spectral density
concepts.definition: Frequency distribution of average power, Fourier-dual to autocorrelation under stated conditions.

concepts.name: Nonparametric spectral estimator
concepts.definition: A finite-data estimate of a spectrum, assessed by bias, variance, leakage, and resolution.

concepts.name: FIR filter
concepts.definition: An LTI filter with a finite impulse response.

concepts.name: Linear phase and group delay
concepts.definition: Phase proportional to frequency, producing constant delay in a passband.

concepts.name: IIR filter
concepts.definition: A recursive filter with an impulse response that can persist indefinitely.

concepts.name: Quantization and finite precision
concepts.definition: Mapping values to a finite set and modeling or bounding the resulting error.

concepts.name: FFT block convolution
concepts.definition: Linear convolution computed in finite FFT blocks with padding and overlap bookkeeping.

concepts.name: Multirate sampling
concepts.definition: Rate change by decimation, interpolation, or rational conversion with anti-alias or anti-image filtering.

concepts.name: Polyphase decomposition
concepts.definition: Partitioning a filter into phase components so computation occurs at the lowest necessary sample rate.

concepts.name: Short-time Fourier transform
concepts.definition: A sequence of windowed spectra indexed by time frame, with overlap conditions governing reconstruction.

concepts.name: Minimum-phase and all-pass factorization
concepts.definition: Factoring a response into minimum-phase magnitude-bearing and all-pass phase-bearing components.

concepts.name: Parametric and subspace spectral estimation
concepts.definition: Spectral inference from ARMA, sinusoidal, covariance, or signal-subspace models.

concepts.name: Perfect-reconstruction filter bank
concepts.definition: An analysis/synthesis bank whose alias and distortion terms cancel exactly up to allowed delay and gain.

concepts.name: Wavelet and constant-Q analysis
concepts.definition: A scale-indexed time-frequency analysis with nonuniform resolution.

concepts.name: Phase vocoder and sinusoidal modeling
concepts.definition: Frame-based spectral modification with phase evolution or tracked sinusoidal parameters.

concepts.name: Finite-wordlength structures and noise shaping
concepts.definition: Structure-dependent coefficient, roundoff, overflow, limit-cycle, and shaped-noise behavior.

concepts.name: Spatial spectrum and array processing
concepts.definition: Spectral estimation over sensor position using array manifolds and spatial covariance.

concepts.name: Multidimensional and image DSP
concepts.definition: Transforms, sampling lattices, filtering, and rate change in two or more dimensions.

canonical_results: Discrete signals are integer-indexed values; delay, reversal, scaling, and addition act on indices or amplitudes in distinct ways.
A finite displayed record is not automatically periodic and is not the underlying physical signal.
Amplitude, normalized frequency, and phase have separable geometric effects.
Frequencies differing by integer multiples of 2pi radians/sample generate identical samples.
Linearity is superposition and time invariance is commutation with shifts.
Causality and BIBO stability are properties to test, not visual impressions from a block diagram.
Every sequence is a weighted sum of shifted impulses.
An LTI system is characterized by h[n] and y[n]=sum_k x[k]h[n-k].
Complex exponentials are eigenfunctions of LTI systems.
Magnitude scales sinusoidal components while phase shifts them; group delay is the negative phase slope.
Sampling replicates a continuous-time spectrum at multiples of the sampling frequency.
Bandlimited reconstruction is exact only when replicas do not overlap and the endpoint convention is handled explicitly.
A uniform quantizer has step q and bounded error; q^2/12 is a model-dependent variance, not a universal deterministic fact.
For a full-scale sinusoid the ideal converter SNR grows by about 6.02 dB per bit under the usual assumptions.
The DTFT is periodic in normalized frequency and turns convolution into multiplication.
Time shifts, modulation, reversal, and conjugation have paired frequency-domain effects with convention-sensitive signs.
The algebraic expression and region of convergence together specify a z-transform.
For a causal rational system, BIBO stability requires poles strictly inside the unit circle; pole-zero geometry predicts magnitude and phase.
The DFT samples one period of a finite record's DTFT under an explicit normalization.
DFT multiplication gives circular convolution; zero-padding to at least P+Q-1 embeds linear convolution.
Factor N into shorter transforms to reduce direct N^2 work to order N log N.
Radix-2 stages use butterflies, permit in-place updates, and introduce a data-order permutation.
Finite observation convolves the true spectrum with the window transform; leakage is not caused by sampling.
Window choice trades main-lobe width, sidelobe height/falloff, scalloping loss, coherent gain, and ENBW.
Randomness is a model for an ensemble, while a finite record is one realization.
For a wide-sense stationary process the PSD and autocorrelation are Fourier pairs, and LTI filtering multiplies PSD by |H|^2.
The raw periodogram is asymptotically unbiased in common settings but not consistent because its variance does not vanish.
Averaging and smoothing reduce variance at the price of resolution; overlap does not create independent records automatically.
Symmetric or antisymmetric FIR coefficients produce linear phase with type-dependent endpoint constraints.
Window, frequency-sampling, least-squares, and equiripple designs optimize different error criteria and are not interchangeable.
Analog-prototype mappings preserve different properties: impulse invariance can alias, while bilinear transformation warps frequency but avoids that aliasing.
Equivalent transfer functions can have sharply different finite-precision behavior, so second-order sections and scaling matter.
OLA and OLS compute acyclic convolution by managing padding, discarded samples, and overlap explicitly.
FFT convolution becomes attractive only beyond a length- and hardware-dependent crossover.
Downsampling replicates and adds spectral images, so anti-alias filtering must precede it.
Upsampling inserts zeros and creates images; rational L/M conversion shares one low-pass filter with gain and band-edge conventions stated.
A filter can be decomposed into phase components without changing its transfer function.
Noble identities move filtering across rate changers so multiplications by inserted zeros or computations later discarded are avoided.
The STFT is simultaneously a sliding windowed DFT and a uniform modulated filter bank.
COLA/WOLA reconstruction depends on the analysis/synthesis window product and hop, not on overlap alone.
Real signals have conjugate-symmetric spectra; analytic signals suppress the negative-frequency half under a declared endpoint convention.
Phase, group delay, and minimum-phase/all-pass structure answer different questions.
coverage_matrix.coverage: core essentials strong; factorization remains extra

canonical_results: A deployed pipeline couples sampling, representation, filtering, estimation, rate change, and finite precision; each idealization has a visible failure mode.
The course capstone must reproduce or audit one real audio, sensor, image, or communication result rather than merely list applications.

prerequisite_graph.direction: Each prerequisites entry points from a lesson to earlier lessons it requires.

core.goal: Compute and visualize basic operations on short discrete signals.
Construct sampled sinusoids and identify an alias pair by inspection and listening.
Classify discrete-time systems by linearity, time invariance, causality, and stability.
Compute an LTI output from its impulse response by convolution.
Represent sampled sinusoids as rotating complex exponentials.
Predict sinusoidal steady-state outputs from an LTI frequency response.
Determine when sampling and ideal reconstruction preserve a bandlimited signal.
Quantify converter error and test when the white-noise model is defensible.
Compute and interpret DTFT representations and their core properties.
Use a z-transform and region of convergence to determine system behavior.
Compute a DFT and distinguish spectral sampling from circular convolution.
Trace a radix-2 FFT and explain its operation count and data ordering.
Select an analysis window from a signal-detection or estimation requirement.
Relate autocorrelation, PSD, and LTI filtering for a stationary random-process model.
Compare periodogram and Welch estimates by bias, variance, leakage, and resolution.
Design and assess a linear-phase FIR filter from frequency specifications.
Design and realize a stable IIR filter while accounting for mapping and structure effects.
Construct an alias-free overlap-add or overlap-save convolution pipeline.
Design anti-alias and anti-image filtering for integer and rational rate change.
Transform a direct rate converter into an efficient polyphase implementation.
Construct and interpret an STFT and spectrogram with declared frame conventions.
Derive and test a WOLA reconstruction condition for frame-domain processing.
Audit and reproduce an end-to-end DSP pipeline against theory, artifacts, and implementation limits.

extras.reason: Spectral factorization and cepstral machinery are valuable but not needed by any core lesson.
ARMA, MUSIC, ESPRIT, Capon, CRB, and model order require linear algebra and statistical assumptions beyond the core estimator outcome.
Paraunitary matrices, spectral factorization, cosine-modulated banks, and wavelets are a coherent advanced branch, not prerequisites for practical resampling or STFT use.
Phase propagation, sinusoidal tracking, and time-scale modification are application depth after reconstructing STFT processing is established.
Limit cycles, noise shaping, sensitivity, and hardware scaling deepen implementation without gating exact-arithmetic core results.
Array manifolds and spatial covariance add geometry and calibration assumptions absent from the one-dimensional core.
Image sampling lattices and multidimensional transforms are applications of the spine, not prerequisites for it.
Linear prediction, Levinson-Durbin, and adaptive estimation need optimization and matrix methods that would overload the core path.

prerequisite_graph.acyclicity_claim: Core nodes are topologically ordered as listed. Every edge points to an earlier core node. Extra nodes depend only on core nodes, and no core node depends on an extra node.

notation_ledger_families.spoken: x at n; delta at n
notation_ledger_families.confusion: Brackets denote discrete indices, not function arguments in continuous time; k is not a physical frequency until f_s and N are supplied.

notation_ledger_families.spoken: x sub c of t; sampling period; sampling frequency
notation_ledger_families.confusion: Reserve parentheses for continuous time and brackets for discrete time; never call n a time in seconds.

notation_ledger_families.spoken: capital omega; omega; f sub k
notation_ledger_families.confusion: Omega is continuous-time angular frequency; omega is dimensionless and 2pi-periodic; k is an index.

notation_ledger_families.spoken: T of x; h at n; x convolved with h
notation_ledger_families.confusion: Use m as a dummy summation index locally only; later decimation factor is uppercase M.

notation_ledger_families.spoken: j; e to the j theta; real part; phase of z
notation_ledger_families.confusion: Use engineering j consistently; phase is modulo 2pi and is undefined at zero magnitude.

symbols: tau_g(omega)=-d angle H/d omega: group delay
notation_ledger_families.spoken: H on the unit circle; magnitude H; group delay
notation_ledger_families.confusion: H(e^(j omega)) is not H(z) without restricting z to the unit circle; group delay is not generally the same as phase delay.

notation_ledger_families.spoken: x transforms to X; X at bin k; W sub N
notation_ledger_families.confusion: Keep DTFT parentheses and DFT brackets distinct; declare the sign and 1/N normalization once and never switch silently.

notation_ledger_families.spoken: X of z; region of convergence; pole p sub i
notation_ledger_families.confusion: The same rational expression can represent different sequences under different ROCs; z_i for a zero must not be confused with the transform variable z.

notation_ledger_families.spoken: w at n; hop R; frame ell
notation_ledger_families.confusion: N is frame/FFT length only when stated; zero padding changes sampled display density, not the window's resolving power.

notation_ledger_families.spoken: expected value; r x x at lag ell; S x x
notation_ledger_families.confusion: A sample average is an estimator of an expectation, not the expectation itself; ell is lag here and frame index only in the STFT family, never in the same subsection.

notation_ledger_families.spoken: passband edge; stopband edge; delta p; A sub s
notation_ledger_families.confusion: Linear ripple and decibels are not interchangeable; state whether a boundary belongs to passband, transition band, or stopband.

notation_ledger_families.spoken: b bits; step q; quantization error
notation_ledger_families.confusion: Do not reuse delta[n] for the quantization step; use q in prose and reserve delta[n] for the impulse.

notation_ledger_families.spoken: down by M; up by L; E sub r
notation_ledger_families.confusion: Downsampling is not anti-alias filtering; upsampling is not interpolation until the anti-image filter is included.

notation_ledger_families.spoken: X at frame ell, bin k; analysis filter k
notation_ledger_families.confusion: State analysis centering, phase convention, normalization, and endpoint treatment; COLA for one window is not automatically WOLA for an analysis/synthesis pair.

advanced_off_path.policy: These topics must be implemented only as extra lessons or starred sections whose removal leaves the core path coherent. No core lesson may list an extra as a prerequisite.
topics: Minimum-phase/all-pass factorization, complex cepstrum, and homomorphic deconvolution
AR/MA/ARMA estimation, linear prediction, model-order criteria, MUSIC, ESPRIT, Capon, APES, and CRB
Paraunitary and linear-phase perfect-reconstruction banks, cosine-modulated banks, and wavelets
Phase vocoder, sinusoidal tracking, source-filter cross-synthesis, and S+N+T models
Coefficient sensitivity, limit cycles, block floating point, sigma-delta/noise shaping, and hardware architecture
Spatial spectra, beamforming, array manifolds, calibration, and direction finding
Two-dimensional transforms, image filtering, sampling lattices, tomography, and multidimensional multirate systems
Adaptive filtering and full linear-prediction algorithms

gaps.gap: No single source gives both a no-prerequisite visual opening and fully qualified sampling/DFT statements.
gaps.response: Use Schaedler for interaction grammar and Smith/Lyons for intuition, then make MIT 6.003/Oppenheim/Osgood the formal correction path by lesson 07.

gaps.gap: Sources use incompatible Fourier signs, scale factors, centered indices, DFT-even conventions, phase origins, and PSD normalizations.
gaps.response: Adopt the notation ledger above, declare conventions in each first exposure, and translate every imported result before use.

gaps.gap: Several sources use dated BASIC, MATLAB/Octave idioms, obsolete hardware, or code links that are no longer dependable.
gaps.response: Reproduce canonical small experiments in current browser-safe or notebook-style code and verify numeric outputs independently.

gaps.gap: No source alone meets the required worked-example pairing, fading, mixed retrieval, complete solutions, boundary probes, and forward-reaching exercise design.
gaps.response: Use MIT problem sets and Oppenheim/Vaidyanathan exercises as task quarries, then rewrite into the project exercise contract with explicit solutions.

gaps.gap: The corpus has many applications but no single compact pipeline that requires the whole proposed core without advanced prerequisites.
gaps.response: Design a measured audio or sensor capstone combining acquisition assumptions, PSD estimation, filtering, rational rate change, STFT inspection, and finite-precision audit.

gaps.gap: Open reading access is not a broad image-reuse license for most books, and several strong source figures carry third-party rights cautions.
gaps.response: Redraw mathematical diagrams as original SVGs, use captured images only after license review, and prefer CC MIT assets or measured/generated plots.

gaps.gap: The canonical list names Oppenheim–Schafer third edition while the complete research summary is the second edition.
gaps.response: Use the researched second-edition section pointers for evidence and verify any final bibliography or changed theorem numbering against the cited edition.

gaps.gap: Audio-heavy and dense spectral figures do not by themselves serve deaf/hard-of-hearing, color-vision-deficient, keyboard-only, or narrow-screen learners.
gaps.response: Pair audio with waveform/spectrum evidence, encode comparisons by shape and labels as well as color, and make every demo keyboard-operable with static explanatory fallback.

redundancies.pattern: DTFT/DFT/FFT fundamentals recur across nearly every textbook.
redundancies.resolution: Choose one derivation spine per result; use alternative sources only for a different representation, counterexample, or exercise.

redundancies.pattern: Many sources repeat long named-window catalogs.
redundancies.resolution: Teach rectangular, Hann, and one adjustable/optimized family through a controlled comparison; move additional families to a reference table or starred section.

redundancies.pattern: FIR and IIR recipes repeat with different notation and software conventions.
redundancies.resolution: Organize by optimization/mapping objective and failure mode, not by source chapter order or catalog completeness.

redundancies.pattern: JOS, MIT 6.341, Orfanidis, Lyons, and Vaidyanathan overlap heavily on decimation, interpolation, and polyphase identities.
redundancies.resolution: Use one practical core derivation, then reserve matrix PR, wavelet, and multidimensional extensions for extras.

redundancies.pattern: Audio, imaging, communications, control, and smoothing examples are abundant but unevenly connected to outcomes.
redundancies.resolution: Keep only applications that cash out a module result or expose a boundary; route others to extras or omit them.

redundancies.pattern: Sources offer multiple metaphors for leakage, convolution, and Fourier coefficients.
redundancies.resolution: Retain at most two coordinated representations per first exposure, then retrieve and reconcile them later rather than stacking analogies at once.
